newsitem.title: USA: Aetna membership declines in third qtr.
newsitem.headline: Aetna membership declines in third qtr.

text.p: Aetna Inc. said on Friday that its total health membership declined in the third quarter with the loss of a large contract, but that premiums grew after its merger with U.S. Healthcare.
It said membership fell to 14.2 million as of September 30, from 14.3 million as of September 30, 1995, due to the loss of the CHAMPUS contract, which covered 700,000 members.
Aetna also said that premiums for the third quarter grew 54 percent to $2.3 billion, reflecting the merger with U.S. Healthcare, compared with $1.5 billion for the third quarter of 1995.

Aetna U.S. Healthcare, which provides managed care, indemnity and group insurance products, said it had operating earnings before amortization of goodwill and other intangibles of $154.7 million in the third quarter, compared with $74.3 million in the prior-year period.

Including amortization of goodwill and other intangibles, Aetna U.S. Healthcare said it had operating earnings of $93.5 million for 1996's third quarter, compared with $71.9 million for the prior-year period.
The third quarter included results from U.S. Healthcare, which merged with Aetna on July 19, whereas 1995 figures only include results from Aetna Health Plans.

The company also said third quarter operating earnings for Aetna International, which sells life insurance and financial products in emerging markets, were $27.2 million, compared with $24.0 million in the third quarter of 1995.

Aetna also said that third quarter operating earnings for Aetna Retirement Services (ARS), which markets life insurance, retirement and investment products, were $49.3 million (excluding the restructuring charge), a 21 percent increase over the $40.7 million reported for the third quarter 1995.

In the third quarter, ARS recorded a $31.8 million after-tax charge for severance and other costs associated with expense reduction and related process redesign efforts in customer service and other business support functions, the company said. Including this charge, operating earnings for the 1996 third quarter were $17.5 million.
The increase in underlying earnings for 1996's third quarter was due primarily to continued growth in assets under management, the company said.
Total assets under management rose 26 percent to $29.9 billion as of September 30, 1996, from $23.8 billion at the end of 1995's third quarter.
